item.title: Virat Kohli birthday: 10 inspiring quotes from the batting superstar
item.description: NEW DELHI: Virat Kohli has inspired people not just with his batting but also with his words. Over the years, his thoughts on hard work, success, self-belief and handling pressure have motivated many young cricketers. Kohli has won almost every major trophy in cricket. His list of titles includes the 50-over World Cup, the T20 World Cup, two Champions Trophy titles and two Indian Premier League (IPL) trophies. He is also India's most successful Test captain. Under his leadership, India won 40 of 68 Tests and lost 17. A look at Virat Kohli's career Kohli has played 123 Tests for India and scored 9,230 runs at an average of 46.85. He has 30 centuries and 31 half-centuries in the format. He is India's fourth-highest run-scorer in Test cricket. In ODIs, Kohli is the world's second-highest run-scorer. He has scored 15,183 runs in 318 matches at an average of 58.84. His tally includes a record 55 centuries and 80 half-centuries. In T20Is, he has scored 4,188 runs in 125 innings at an average of 48.69. He has one century and 38 half-centuries. Across all three formats, Kohli has scored 28,601 runs in 566 matches. His average is 52.86. He has 86 centuries and 149 half-centuries, with a highest score of 254 not out. He is the second-highest run-scorer in international cricket. As Kohli celebrates his 38th birthday on Thursday, here are some of his best quotes. 135563679 Virat Kohli's quotes Self-belief and hard work will always earn you success. I never stop working. I never stop trying to improve. That is my mantra. There is no shortcut to success. I love playing under pressure. In fact, if there's no pressure, then I'm not in the perfect zone. I like to be myself, and I don't pretend. For instance, I don't dress up for occasions; I am what I am. A fit body gives you confidence. And there's nothing more impressive than a great attitude, which you can wear on your sleeve. You learn everyday, you try to improve everyday.

item.title: Pirates prospect Wyatt Sanford selected to AFL All-Star team
item.description: UNITED STATES - OCTOBER 11: Wyatt Sanford #3 of the Glendale Desert Dogs throws during the game between the Desert Dogs and the Saguaros at Surprise Stadium on Sunday, October 11, 2026 in Surprise, AZ United States. (Photo by Jill Weisleder/Minor League Baseball via Getty Images) The Pittsburgh Pirates have yet another budding star developing into one of the sport’s best prospects, as Wyatt Sanford has earned an invitation to the Arizona Fall League All-Star team. Sanford has been one of the best hitters in the AFL this season and that started from his very first contest with the Glendale Desert Dogs. In his first game in Arizona the Frisco Texas product went deep for his first homer of the Fall league. Sanford would match that power with the longest homer of his career on October 22 when he hit a 454 foot shot to centerfield off a 95 mph fastball. Sanford’s power has been on display all year as he went from only hitting five last season to clobbering 19 in 2026. In addition to his power at the plate, Sanford has been a consistent threat at the plate and has been very efficient during his time in the desert. The 20-year old shortstop is hitting 283/.386/.417 through 15 games. In that span he’s scored 13 runs and has had 17 hits, two doubles, nine RBIs and was walked nine times. For a predominantly defensive first infielder, he’s grown very quickly into a confident hitter. Wyatt Sanford has been named a Fall Star in the Arizona Fall League. Catch up with Wyatt talking to @AlexJStumpf while there https://t.co/yoyMdNaYLD https://t.co/9y4yJIgidf — 𝐍𝐒𝟗 (@NorthShoreNine) November 4, 2026 Sanford spoke with Alex Stumpf of North Shore Nine and discussed his development as a hitter and the adjustments he made in the weight room and at the plate. “This year was definitely a big confidence boost for sure. It felt really good coming up to the plate with an extra tool this year and I think it’s just going to propel me in my career with the years coming,” Sanford said. “Working on becoming a complete hitter down here. Had a lot of swing-and-misses here so trying to refine that while I’m here and if I can refine that, I’ll be a good little player.” As the fifth-ranked Pirates’ prospect, there will be a lot of eyes on Sanford, especially after the showcase he’s put on in the AFL. He was the only Pirate to be selected to the AFL All-Star team this season. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces international retirement
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo is retiring after playing 234 times for Portugal (Fayez NURELDINE) Portuguese football legend Cristiano Ronaldo announced on Thursday that he was retiring from international football. The 41-year-old, who has played 234 times for Portugal and scored 146 goals, fell out with national coach Jorge Jesus last month after he refused to use him in a Nations League match. Ronaldo immediately left the team camp. "To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team," Ronaldo said in a video on his Instagram account. "I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world," he continued. obo/gj/lp

item.title: Crystal Palace receive double injury boost ahead of Liverpool clash
item.description: Crystal Palace receive double injury boost ahead of Liverpool clash Liverpool in Turkey: Fenerbahce Fightback Exposes Problems Before Crystal Palace Trip Liverpool lost again in Turkey, and there is no need to dress it up. Fenerbahce came from behind to win late, with Vedat Muriqi delivering the decisive goal after another erratic defensive showing. The game had enough warning signs before the score moved. Kostas Tsimikas was fortunate to avoid heavier punishment after shoving Mason Greenwood in the box. Liverpool then went ahead anyway, Trey Nyoni opening the scoring with a deflected effort. It lasted four minutes. Greenwood replied, also via a deflection, and the pattern was set, Liverpool threatening in moments, vulnerable for long stretches. Alexander Isak, introduced from the bench, looked to have tilted it back Liverpool’s way when he made it 2-1. That should have been the platform to close the game out. Instead, Liverpool folded. Archie Brown equalised, Muriqi struck late, and Fenerbahce completed a comeback that felt entirely avoidable. Photo: IMAGO Fenerbahce comeback leaves Liverpool with questions There were positives in flashes. Nyoni continues to show composure, Isak changed the tempo, and Liverpool still carried a threat. The larger point remains simple, this side gave up too much control and paid for it. In a hostile away setting, that tends to happen. Now the focus shifts quickly to Crystal Palace and the Premier League. Liverpool head to Selhurst Park on Sunday, where Pierre Sage has at least been given better news on the fitness front. Quinten Timber and Jorgen Strand Larsen are both expected back in contention after missing time since Palace’s last European outing. Sage said: “Both [players] will be back with us. They were training with us last week but not ready to play, but now they are ready to play. All [others] will be okay.” Crystal Palace injury boost adds edge to Selhurst Park test Palace are still in trouble. They sit 18th in the Premier League with seven points from nine matches and have lost their last three league games, conceding nine without scoring. Even so, returns in midfield and attack matter. Liverpool are coming off a collapse, Palace are desperate, and that usually means a difficult afternoon. For Andoni Iraola, the issue is not the result in isolation. It is the softness around key moments. Liverpool created enough to get something in Turkey. They also made enough mistakes to leave with nothing.

item.title: LIV Golf demise edging closer, says South Australian premier
item.description: FILE PHOTO - First place individual champion, Anthony Kim of 4Aces GC, Captain Jon Rahm of Legion XIII and Tyrrell Hatton of Legion XIII, stand on the podium during the trophy ceremony after the final round of the LIV Golf Adelaide tournament at Grange Golf Club. (is associated with: «LIV Golf demise edging closer, says South Australian premier») Chris Trotman/LIV Golf/dpa LIV Golf’s anticipated demise has moved a step closer, with South Australia Premier Peter Malinauskas suggesting it was “game, set and match” for the breakaway circuit. Four LIV events have been held in state capital Adelaide but Malinauskas cast doubt over the viability of the next competition that was due to take place at Kooyonga Golf Club in March, as well as the wider tournament. The Financial Times has reported that BC Partners Credit, who had been lined up as potential backers following the withdrawal of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, have pulled out of a deal worth more almost $300 million due to an exodus of star players. LIV had been forced to apply for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the US, effectively cancelling playing contracts, with three-time champion Jon Rahm departing, while the likes of Sergio Garcia, Ian Poulter, Tyrrell Hatton, Louis Oosthuizen and Lee Westwood are among those who see their future elsewhere. While there has been no formal confirmation of liquidation, Malinauskas offered a pessimistic take. He told ABC Adelaide: “It feels like it’s game, set and match as far as I can tell. “That’s because BC Partners, that is the funders of LIV 2.0, I guess, have arrived at the same conclusion that we were (at): if you don’t get the players to sign up, then it doesn’t go ahead. “Clearly the event, as far as we can tell, won’t be going ahead at Kooyonga next year.” Speaking at a news conference, he added: “We’ve seen reports that BC Partners don’t intend to support LIV if they don’t get the players that are required, which is essentially consistent with the South Australian government’s position we’ve communicated to LIV for a while. “I have reached out to LIV Golf over the last couple of hours and sought confirmation myself. It’s fair to say on all accounts, on all information we have before us, I think it’s not going to happen next year.” World number two Rory McIlroy, who has been a vocal critic of the project from the start, offered a withering assessment of developments at a press conference ahead of this week’s Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship. “They took players, they took sponsors, they turned professional golf into an arms race. item.title: Alexander Zverev ‘annoyed’ by reaction to him becoming men’s world No 1
item.description: Alexander Zverev says he is “annoyed” by the reaction to him becoming men’s world No 1 in the last few weeks. The 29-year-old German, who had a breakthrough season after claiming his first two Grand Slams at the French Open and US Open, insists he is the only player who “has to explain why it’s OK” for him to be at the top of the rankings. Zverev, who was knocked out of the Paris Masters by Lorenzo Musetti on Wednesday, did not specify what has actually annoyed him. His table-topping achievement has come in a year blighted by injuries for Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz , who won the last nine majors prior to Roland Garros . Zverev also becomes the first year-end world No 1 to not win a single Masters 1000 tournament despite playing in every event. "I don't think anybody had to explain themselves as much as I had to do in the last couple of days, which for me, is annoying, to be honest," Zverev said. "I was a bit annoyed, to be honest, because achieving the world number one status is something that every player dreams of. "But then I feel like I'm the only world number in tennis history that has to explain why it's OK for me to be world number one, which I find quite difficult, because I think I deserve to be where I am, even though I lost today." Zverev has a 62-8 win-loss record against players ranked outside the top-10 this year but has actually only won three out of 12 matches against top-10 players. Zverev receives a trophy for finishing the year as world No 1 (Getty) The two-time major winner has also had his reputation impacted in recent years by allegations of physical abuse from two former partners. Zverev has always denied the accusations and insists they are baseless. Zverev lost 7-5(5), 6-2 to Italian world No 24 Musetti and said of his performance: "To simplify it, he played really good and I played really bad. "I think this was not a very good match from me, I think it might be one of the worst in the last couple of months." Zverev will now focus on the ATP Finals in Turin and the Davis Cup Finals in Bologna as he looks to close his season on a high.

item.title: Tom Brady explains what ‘sold’ him about putting Chicago Bears top of his NFL power rankings
item.description: Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images The Chicago Bears have been in great form of late and most recently secured a win over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 8. The Bears are now 6-2 for the season and they have earned top spot in Tom Brady’s NFL power rankings after the latest round of games. When revealing his rankings to Fox Sports, Brady did say that he initially had the Buffalo Bills in first place when he was thinking about his list. However, he goes on to say that there is ‘something about the vibe in Chicago’ that ‘sold’ him on putting the Bears ahead of the Bills. Brady said: “I had them [the Bills] at number one when I first started thinking about this list. They’re definitely deserving, but I had another idea. “Well, last week I asked if Chicago could go from five to one with a win in Seattle, and I’m a man of my word. “The Bears went into Seattle on Monday night and handled their business. D’Andre Swift scored three times, and when Seattle made it a one-score game late, Chicago answered and oh yeah, Jeffery Simmons is anchoring the defence from now on. No big deal, right? Look, these are power rankings, not standings. And there’s something about the vibe in Chicago that sold me on giving them the top spot. “But with great power comes great responsibility, right? Let’s see what Caleb can do next.” The Bears are now preparing to take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers this coming Sunday. Tampa are 3-5 for the season and beat the Atlanta Falcons in their Week 8 matchup. item.title: Niklas Scheller signs professional terms
item.description: Niklas Scheller signs professional terms Eintracht Frankfurt have handed homegrown youngster Niklas Scheller a professional contract. The 18-year-old has been with the Eagles since 2018. Niklas Scheller has become the latest youngster from the Eintracht Frankfurt academy to sign professional terms with the Eagles. After starting out at boyhood club SC Dortelweil, Scheller played for FV Bad Vilbel and FSV Frankfurt before moving to the Riederwald in 2018, initially as an U11 player. The centre-back, who grew up just north of Frankfurt, rose through the youth ranks before making the step up to the U21s this summer – despite the fact he was still eligible to represent the Eagles’ U19 side. Scheller was also one of several youngsters included in the Eintracht first team’s pre-season training camp in Grassau. Having already made his U21 debut in the fifth-tier Hessenliga last season, Scheller is now a key member of Eintracht’s squad in the Regionalliga Südwest – the fourth tier of German football. His performances have not gone unnoticed at international level, where he has been included in Germany’s U19 squad for their upcoming fixtures this month. Last year, he was called up by his country for the U17 World Cup. Sporting director Timmo Hardung said: “After returning from injury this spring, Niklas has made very good progress and quickly established himself in the men’s game. He’s a local boy and a shining example of our philosophy in developing players at the youth academy. As part of the U21 team, Niklas continues to have the opportunity to play regularly at a high level, so he can gradually work his way towards meeting the demands of professional football.” Alexander Richter, head of Eintracht’s youth academy, added: “As a player who is still eligible for the U19s, Niklas is really demonstrating his potential in the Regionalliga this season. He is stepping up to shoulder responsibility in a league filled mostly with older, more experienced players, and he has quickly adapted to the pace of the game and physicality of the challenges. We’re delighted to be able to offer another homegrown, regional youngster a clear pathway and will continue to support him in his development as best we can.”

item.title: Adam Schefter shares the ‘biggest name’ who could be traded in the NFL before the deadline
item.description: Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images Adam Schefter has given an Indianapolis Colts answer about which big NFL star could yet be traded before the deadline. The NFL trade deadline is on November 10, with under a week left for teams to pick up players to help them in the second half of the season. Some big names have already been on the move, Jeffery Simmons being the biggest example. The Indianapolis Colts are starting over, and as such, have been sellers during this period after firing Chris Ballard. DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson have both been traded already. According to Adam Schefter, another Colts star is the biggest name around the league at risk of being moved. Adam Schefter on Jonathan Taylor being the biggest name on the market, and how it might affect Breece Hall The Colts are going into a complete rebuild, and as such, their star running back is hardly on their timeline. There have been reports suggesting that the ownership does not want to move Jonathan Taylor, but an offer might come in which is too good to turn down. The 27-year-old is a 3-time Pro Bowl selection, having led the NFL in rushing touchdowns in two different seasons. He would fetch a good price. The league insider thinks it might just end up happening. “Jonathan Taylor is the biggest name out there, could be traded at any point in time,” Schefter said on his podcast . “My read on that is that the Indianapolis Colts have offers from teams. They’re going to wait to see if these teams sweeten the offers, if they can get a better offer. And I think in the end, whether it’s today, this week, next week, I think in the end they decide to move Jonathan Taylor. That’s my guess. “I think in the end they decide to move Josh Downs. But I think the thing to watch at this time of the year with the trade deadline approaching, I’m watching the players on those teams that are not talked about as much. We’re talking about Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs. What about Breece Hall? “Yeah. Again, Aaron Glenn on Monday said, We’re not looking to trade Breece Hall. But we have the Vikings, Giants, Broncos, Packers, others interested in Jonathan Taylor. They’re all not going to get Jonathan Taylor. One team might get Jonathan Taylor. One team. So what happens if and when Jonathan Taylor is traded? Who’s the next running back that teams are going to be calling on? Breece Hall.” It would certainly be some statement from the Colts to move on from Taylor as well. Cashing in while his price is high and there are multiple suitors does sound like the best idea. It would be far from a surprise to see Indianapolis move on from their star. item.title: Liam Livingstone moves to CSK for a reduced salary: Explaining the finances and auction purse impact in CSK-SRH four-player trade
item.description: Liam Livingstone moves to CSK for a reduced salary: Explaining the finances and auction purse impact in CSK-SRH four-player trade originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Liam Livingstone accepts a ₹7 crore pay cut to join Chennai Super Kings after a poor season. Sunrisers Hyderabad gain a ₹9.20 crore purse boost while Chennai’s shrinks by ₹2.20 crore. Chennai add power and spin, while Hyderabad strengthen their pace attack and free overseas slots. MORE: IPL 2027 trade tracker: Complete list of all player and cash deals Explained: The financial math behind CSK’s 4-player trade with SRH for Liam Livingstone Liam Livingstone has agreed to play for Chennai Super Kings at less than half of the salary Sunrisers Hyderabad paid for him a year ago, and the arithmetic behind that move says a great deal about how IPL trades are priced. The England all-rounder has dropped from ₹13 crore to ₹6 crore, and the way the two franchises’ purses have been adjusted shows why one side comes out far better off on paper. The deal is a four-player swap. Chennai receive Livingstone at ₹6 crore and the Australian all-rounder Jack Edwards at ₹3 crore, while Hyderabad take left-arm pacer Khaleel Ahmed at ₹4.8 crore and Nathan Ellis, the Australian quick, at ₹2 crore. Contracts normally travel with a player at their auction value in a trade, but the fee can be revised if the player consents in writing, both franchises agree, and the IPL Governing Council ratifies the change. Livingstone had little leverage. He played only two matches in IPL 2026, scored 15 runs and lost his place in Hyderabad’s playing XI, so a release into the auction pool looked likely, and overseas all-rounders in poor form often see steep price falls or go unsold. A guaranteed ₹6 crore deal with a franchise known for clear roles was the safer choice. The figures matter because the mini-auction is close, and every crore counts for a franchise that wants to shape its squad. A trade of this kind does more than move four players, since it also changes how much each team can spend when the bidding opens. The two sides therefore finish the exchange in very different positions, with Hyderabad holding a comfortable cushion and Chennai carrying a modest debit. item.title: Kane picks trophies over Premier League record or NFL with Bayern deal
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Bayern Munich's Harry Kane celebrates scoring his side's second goal during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Bayern Munich and Arsenal at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Kane picks trophies over Premier League record or NFL with Bayern deal») Sven Hoppe/dpa Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane will stay at the club until 2029 at least, meaning Alan Shearer and NFL kickers can breathe a sigh of relief. Kane is 33 and could play at the highest level for longer than most forwards given pace has never been his main asset. Even so, committing to the Bundesliga champions for two more years makes it less likely that the recent Ballon d'Or winner will be able to pursue two other sporting dreams. He is on 213 Premier League goals and had Shearer's record of 260 is his sights before he opted to leave Tottenham Hotspur for Bayern in 2023 in search of trophies - something he had never won in England. He had to wait a season with perennial champions Bayern giving up their crown for one campaign to Bayer Leverkusen in 2024, but two subsequent Bundesliga titles, a German Cup and now the personal honour of being voted the world's best male footballer means Germany will remain his home. "My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay," Kane, who will be almost 36 by the end of the contract, said in a statement on Thursday. "I'm now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club." The striker has scored 156 goals in 161 competitive appearances for Bayern, breaking records along the way. His previous deal was due to run out in June. Given he is morphing into a number 10, with his assists of late just as impressive as his goals, Kane could theoretically play until around his 40s as injuries have never played a big role in his career. The average retirement age for an English footballer is 35. But if the captain stopped playing for England after the home Euros in 2028 - where he has a strong shot at ending the national team's long trophy hoodoo - Kane could extend his club career further. NFL kicker dream That might leave a window to return to England with Tottenham or a lesser light such as Fulham to try to conquer Shearer's record from the latter's time at Southampton, Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle United in the 1990s and 2000s. It still looks unlikely though that he would score enough goals in a probable period of diminishing returns for an ageing forward to reach 260. Another reason Shearer can sleep easy is Kane's open flirtation with one day wanting to try out as an NFL kicker. His love of American Football is well known, as is the league's penchant for money-spinning marketing and publicity. "That is something I will try and look at a bit more seriously," Kane said in September. "It all depends on what happens in my career over the next five or six years, the motivation and what I want to do. "The NFL is a lot more realistic than the golf one, let's put it that way." item.title: 3 biggest takeaways for Sixers following big road win over Pistons
item.description: DETROIT -- The Philadelphia 76ers made a statement as they went into Little Caesars Arena on Wednesday and defeated the Detroit Pistons by a score of 112-106 . The Sixers led by as many as 18 and maintained their lead for a majority of the game as they put a stop to plenty of runs the Pistons tried to make in this one. Jaylen Brown was terrific and led the Sixers with 30 points and seven rebounds, Joel Embiid had 26 points and 15 rebounds, and LeBron James added 13 points, 10 rebounds, and eight assists. VJ Edgecombe had 11 points and six rebounds and Tyrese Maxey had 19 and seven assists. Here are the three biggest takeaways following the win in Detroit: Brown seals the game As fantastic as Brown was on the offensive end, it was the defensive end in which he sealed the game. The Pistons had all the momentum as they had pulled to within 106-102. After Embiid missed a top-of-the-key triple, Ausar Thompson rebounded the miss and pushed it up to star guard Cade Cunningham. Detroit's leader had his eye on a wing 3-pointer to attempt to pull the Pistons to within one with still plenty of time to go, but Brown made a phenomenal defensive play to reject his 3-point attempt and allow the Sixers to seal the win. The block was deflating one for Detroit and it was a defensive play that shocked the Little Caesars Arena crowd. "Yeah, it was big," coach Nick Nurse said of the block. "I think Jaylen, obviously, had a good game, made another play. We were just kind of trying to trying to finish the game, and we needed to keep making a few more plays down the down the stretch there. That was certainly a huge one." Maxey shakes free late The Pistons have an elite defensive stopper in the form of Thompson and he did a terrific job on Maxey all night long. He forced him into some tough looks, held him in check for a majority of the night, but the 2-time All-Star on his 26th birthday finally broke free in the fourth quarter as he scored 11 of his 19 in the final frame to get the job done. He also only had one turnover on the night and had seven assists despite shooting just 5-for-16 on the night. Before finally getting into an offensive rhythm, Maxey was able to do a number of other things to help Philadelphia finish the job, especially on the defensive end. "I liked the way he played," Nurse added. "He had a seven assist, one turnover game. They're, obviously, scheming for him, and I thought he played pretty comfortable, to be honest, and I like that more than anything." Scoring depth This was an example of Philadelphia's star power. The Pistons deserve credit for being able to take Maxey out of the game a bit, but the Sixers still built a double-digit lead because of all of the other options they can turn to on that end of the floor. item.title: David Raya admits Arsenal was “a little bit surprised” by Slavia’s second half
item.description: David Raya admits Arsenal was “a little bit surprised” by Slavia’s second half David Raya has admitted that Arsenal were surprised by Slavia Praha’s response in the second half of their Champions League meeting last night, as the hosts made life difficult for the Gunners after the interval. Arsenal entered the fixture following a morale boosting victory over Liverpool at the weekend, and there were expectations that they would carry that confidence into another comfortable performance. Their first half display appeared to justify that optimism, as they controlled the game and established a 2-0 lead before the break. However, the contest changed significantly after half time. Slavia Praha raised their intensity and became much more aggressive, putting Arsenal under pressure and forcing the visitors into mistakes. The Gunners struggled to retain possession and lost several balls they would normally expect to win. Slavia Praha make Arsenal work for victory Arsenal eventually held on to secure a 2-1 victory and returned to North London with all three points. Nevertheless, their performance after the break exposed areas that will need attention, particularly their ability to respond when opponents increase the pressure. Slavia Praha deserve credit for their determination and the way they approached the second half. They refused to accept defeat and pushed Arsenal into serious difficulty, creating the possibility of a much more damaging result for the visitors. The Czech side could arguably have made even more of their opportunities, but their response demonstrated how difficult away matches in the Champions League can become when the opposition finds another level. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) Raya admits Arsenal were surprised Speaking after the match, Raya acknowledged that Arsenal had not expected such a strong response from their opponents. The goalkeeper told Sky Sports : “First half, we played really really well. We dominated the whole game, created a lot of chances and could have scored a few more goals. “The second half it was a completely different half. From them, they put up a gear. We were a little bit surprised and they made it really difficult for us – which we have to learn from. We know important are away games are and how difficult places like this [can be]. They became man-to-man all over the pitch.” Raya’s comments underline the importance of Arsenal learning from the experience. Winning away from home in Europe requires more than a strong opening period, and the Gunners must find a way to maintain control when opponents change their approach. item.title: YouTube Gold: Jay Bilas Addresses The Team
item.description: W e can’t say for sure that he does it every year, because we don’t keep track of it when he does, but Jay Bilas seems to address Duke’s teams at or near the beginning of each season. He did it again this year, opening with the famous quote from John F. Kennedy’s inaugural address: ask not what your country can do for you. Ask what you can do for your country. That was the framework of his comments. Here are some more excerpts: “I can tell you one thing about being older is that’s where regret is, and regret lasts forever. You don’t want to be in a position where you’re going to regret not putting everything you had into this team this season. There’s never been a player here that has regretted putting everything they had in. There have been players here that regret not doing that.” “If you look at some of the great teams that have played here that have won championships, not one of them could tell you how many minutes guys played on the roster, how many points everybody scored. They’re not going to remember any of that. They’re going to remember the contributions that their teammates made and how much they admired what their teammates did.” “The only truth that matters is the truth that is in this room. You’re going to have schlubs like me that are going to be commenting on what you’re doing. Your families have a certain view of it. Your agent, the media, there’s going to be a lot of talk. None of that means anything. The only thing that matters is what you guys think and what you guys do and how you relate to one another as teammates.” It’s always great to hear these speeches. It’s comforting definitely having 13 out there and looking forward to seeing whenever he gets a chance, whether it’s this week or down the road to get back. We can hear him back out there on the field today just talking it up,” Maye said. Hollins had made an encouraging start to the season before his injury, recording 15 receptions for 209 yards across his first four games. He averaged 13.9 yards per reception during that stretch. The 33-year-old also offers New England another physical presence in the passing game and as a blocker, giving the offence greater flexibility. His return is particularly important with the Patriots dealing with several injuries at wide receiver. A.J. Brown missed the 24-19 victory over the Miami Dolphins after experiencing setbacks with his ankle and knee, while Romeo Doubs remains on injured reserve with a shoulder injury. Brown also missed practice, leaving his availability against Green Bay uncertain. Head coach Mike Vrabel had previously suggested Hollins could return this week, although he stressed that the receiver must be ready physically. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Hollins’ return to practice opened a 21-day window for New England to activate him from injured reserve. The Patriots can bring him back at any point during that period, meaning Maye could have his trusted target available for the Packers clash. item.description: Five Things Learned: RB Leipzig 2-3 Manchester City (UEFA Champions League) The first-half was studied between both sides as Antonio Nusa almost scored from distance, a quarter of an hour after Gianluigi Donnarumma failed to keep hold of the ball from a long-distance effort, and fortunately parried it backwards and over the crossbar. However, one player who did hit his own goal was RB Leipzig’s Castello Lukeba, making a mess inside the box and deflecting Nico O’Reilly’s cross via his knee on 37 minutes, opening the scoring for Manchester City . The visitors' first attempt on target actually came two minutes after Lukeba’s error, as Erling Haaland headed a weak effort from a cross into the hands of goalkeeper Martin Vandervoort. After the half-time break, Martin Demichelis’ Leipzig imposed their game with Donnarumma making a stunning save to deny Brajan Gruda on 47 minutes, only to offer an open net from a tight angle for Ridle Baku to score the equaliser 120 seconds later. The response was fast, however, as Iliman Ndiaye cut inside from the left and placed a perfect cross onto the head of Enzo Fernandez , who directed the ball home 10 minutes later. RB Leipzig would then reply even quicker as Antonio Nusa levelled things up inside the box three minutes after Manchester City had regained the lead. But when the visitors need him most, Erling Haaland is usually there to finish, and the Norwegian capped off a fantastic piece of play by Elliot Anderson to secure the winner on the 78th minute. There was still time for both RB Leipzig and City to hit the crossbar, although the match would end in a thrilling 2-3 away win for the Blues, leaving Enzo Maresca’s men in seventh position (automatic round of 16 spot), with nine points from a possible 12 so far. item.title: Nnamdi Collins: Man United face major hurdle in pursuit of Eintracht Frankfurt defender
item.description: Nnamdi Collins: Man United face major hurdle in pursuit of Eintracht Frankfurt defender Manchester United may have signed three defenders in the summer of 2024, but they are preparing for another defensive revamp in 2027. The Red Devils added Matthijs de Ligt, Leny Yoro and Noussair Mazraoui to their squad before the start of the 2024/25 campaign. While Yoro has been on the rise of late, De Ligt has suffered with injuries, while Mazraoui is not a guaranteed starter at Old Trafford. Elsewhere, Harry Maguire is in the final phase of his career and his contract expires next summer. Lisandro Martinez’s future also remains uncertain after the public outburst last month aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. United are 17th in the Premier League table after nine games this season and have conceded 15 times in the league. The Red Devils are preparing to address the backline next year, with several candidates also being linked to the club in January. It now appears that the English giants have set their sights on a Bundesliga defender. Page 1 of 4 1 2 3 4 United want Nnamdi Collins According to Fussball News , United have identified Eintracht Frankfurt defender Nnamdi Collins as a target. The report states: “Eintracht Frankfurt appears to be facing growing interest in Nnamdi Collins. According to information from fussball-news.de, Manchester United, Chelsea FC and Liverpool FC are all taking a keen interest in the Frankfurt defender.” “All three Premier League clubs are monitoring his progress and have the German youth international regularly scouted.” However, the report insists that the Bundesliga club have no desire to let him leave in January, after having recently tied him down to a new deal until 2030. Fast, athletic and with the ability to play at centre-back as well as right-back, the German defender is adept at dealing with pacey attackers. He is particularly good in one-on-one situations, where his blistering speed and strength give him an added advantage. No offers yet Collins ‘ efforts have already turned heads in England, with the report adding: “According to information from fussball-news.de, the 22-year-old was scouted, amongst other things, whilst playing for the German Under-21 national team against Georgia.” The 22-year-old’s suitors are also keeping an eye on his performances in the DFB Pokal and the Bundesliga. Meanwhile, the Premier League trio remain firmly in the race but are yet to submit a concrete offer for Collins. Instead, interest from United and Co. is believed to be at the scouting phase, with the clubs assessing the player’s suitability to their squad reinforcement plans. For the Red Devils, the move is a no-brainer, given their poor form at the back. Frankfurt want €35 million While Frankfurt are averse to a winter exit, a move at the end of the season cannot be entirely ruled out. However, it could be a costly affair as the German club are likely to demand at least €35 million for his signature, apart from add-ons.
